displayName: BDE Confirmation (shop-floor booking, one row per confirmation)
description: The CONFIRMATION grain of the sim-v5 BDE feed, alongside and NOT replacing SMProfile-OperationsResponse. Full text: docs/history/standard/profiles/operations/bde-confirmation.md, description.

properties.name: confirmation_no
properties.description: The booking's own identity (e.g. BDE-2026-08-03-2208427). UNIQUE per confirmation — this is what makes the grain safe to key, where production_order_no repeats.

properties.name: production_order_no
properties.description: The production order this booking confirms (RESPONDS_TO). NOT the identity at this grain — many confirmations share one order.

refStatus.reason: The reference is kept as a value: core 2.0.0 has no edge for it yet.

properties.name: article_revision
properties.description: The revision of the article that was built or used, where the source's article number carries none (a PLM part number with revision A). Empty when the number itself names the revision (at SAP dddd.1).

properties.name: machine_ref
properties.description: Executing machine (machine_no). MEASURED 2026-08-03: non-null on 2000 of 2000 rows at this grain across 81 distinct values, where the per-production-order aggregate carries it on only 32 of 100. The machine binding survives here and is lost there.

refStatus.reason: The machine of a confirmation is its SegmentResponse's EquipmentActual — the edge lives there (SMProfile-SegmentResponse ACTUAL_EQUIPMENT); an edge from here would be a shortcut through SegmentResponse (retired 25.09.). Kept as a value (Explorer X1, judged core 6.0.0).

properties.name: operation_no
properties.description: The routing operation (Arbeitsgang) this booking belongs to. MEASURED: 1714 of 2000 rows, 30 distinct. Absent on the rest — a booking without an operation is not an error here, and it must stay absent rather than default to a first operation.

properties.name: shift
properties.description: Shift of record for the booking, derived upstream from machine_departments x machine_pools x shift_config x shift_weekly_pattern (sim-v5, 2026-08-03). Full text: docs/history/standard/profiles/operations/bde-confirmation.md, attributes › shift › description.

properties.name: good_qty
properties.description: Pieces booked as good on this confirmation.

properties.name: scrap_qty
properties.description: Pieces booked as scrap on this confirmation. The ERP half of the quantity axis — the counterpart the machine's own part_scrap counter is reconciled against.

properties.name: rework_qty
properties.description: Pieces booked for rework — a THIRD disposition, deliberately not folded into scrap (same rule as the part_scrap semantic in standard/mappings/attribute-aliases.json). Full text: docs/history/standard/profiles/operations/bde-confirmation.md, attributes › rework_qty › description.

properties.name: scrap_reason
properties.description: Reason code for the scrap on this booking. MEASURED: only 123 of 2000 rows carry one, with 2 distinct values (cavity-defect, quality-fail). Thin by nature — most bookings have no scrap at all — so a consumer must treat absence as 'no reason recorded', never as a category.

properties.name: labor_min
properties.description: Personnel minutes booked against this confirmation. Full text: docs/history/standard/profiles/operations/bde-confirmation.md, attributes › labor_min › description.

properties.name: machine_min
properties.description: Machine minutes booked against this confirmation.

properties.name: setup_min
properties.description: Setup minutes booked against this confirmation. MEASURED: non-zero on 25 of 800 rows — setup is an event, not a per-booking constant, so a zero here is a real 'no setup on this booking'.

properties.name: cycle_time_actual_sec
properties.description: Actually measured cycle time per piece (s) for this booking.

properties.name: actual_start_time
properties.description: Start of the booked interval (ts_start). Absent at the per-production-order grain.

properties.name: updated_at
properties.description: Last change (recorded_at). Server-managed and volatile on every read.

properties.name: operations_type
properties.description: ISA-95 operations type (B2MML OperationsType; Part 3/4: which MOM area the object belongs to; audit M1). A source without the column sets the constant of the profile's momDomain (columnMappings const).

isa95.note: ISA-95 places the shop-floor booking under Operations Response (its segment response). This profile is the per-booking grain of that object: one row is one booking (key confirmation_no); SMProfile-OperationsResponse is the per-request aggregate. Both are Level-3 actuals.
isa95.mappingNote: B2MML SegmentResponse has one quantity per material actual, no good/scrap/rework split, no scrap reason, no shift, no booked minutes and no cycle time; operation_no is the ERP routing operation number, no B2MML ID; updated_at is a technical timestamp of the source. Audit M3 (core 6.0.0): good_qty is the produced MaterialActual (MaterialUse Produced), labor_min / machine_min the personnel / equipment actual quantity (UoM MIN); scrap_qty and rework_qty stay ours — B2MML 0701 has no MaterialUse for scrap or rework (each would need a MaterialDefinition of its own); setup_min belongs to a segment response of its own. PLM as-built (owner 29.10.2026): article_revision names the state that was built where the source's id carries none; B2MML references a definition by its ID alone (an ID means one state), so there is no field for it — an extension, never part of the key.
